summary: Namco's MotoGP/500cc Grand Prix motorcycle racing line, beginning with the 500GP arcade cabinet and continuing through PlayStation 2 entries before Capcom's PS2-only MotoGP '07.

entries.title: 500GP

emulation.notes: Use original hardware where possible; no sourced home version exists.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Namco Super System 23 arcade presentation with physical cabinet controls

primary.version: Original Namco Super System 23 arcade release
primary.why: 500GP is sourced as a Namco arcade motorcycle racer on Super System 23 hardware, based on the 1998 500cc Grand Prix season and later reworked into the first MotoGP console entry. With no sourced home port, the arcade cabinet is the only complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original arcade hardware or a legally configured arcade-preservation setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not confuse 500GP with GP 500, the separate PC game released around the same era.

entries.title: MotoGP

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 or original PlayStation 2 hardware.

primary.why: Namco's MotoGP is sourced as a PlayStation 2-only game based on the 1999 season and on Namco's 500GP arcade game. It includes guest unlocks such as Klonoa and Gun Koma, with no other platform documented.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscaling.

entries.remaster_caveats: Distinct from THQ's MotoGP: Ultimate Racing Technology line.

entries.title: MotoGP 2

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 or original PlayStation 2 hardware.

primary.why: Namco's MotoGP 2 is sourced as a PlayStation 2-only sequel based on the 2001 Grand Prix motorcycle racing season, adding five tracks, wet-weather racing, legends mode, and improved rider models/animation. It is separate from THQ's similarly named PC/Xbox MotoGP 2.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscaling.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate with MotoGP: Ultimate Racing Technology 2, the THQ/Climax PC/Xbox/mobile game.

entries.title: MotoGP 3

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 or original PlayStation 2 hardware.

primary.why: Namco's MotoGP 3 is sourced as a PlayStation 2-only game based on the 2002 MotoGP season, with 15 real-world circuits, fantasy layouts, custom riders, challenge unlocks, legends, and Namco guest riders. With no other platform documented, PS2 is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on PlayStation 2 hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscaling.

entries.remaster_caveats: Distinct from other publishers' MotoGP games with similar names.

entries.title: MotoGP 4

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 or original PlayStation 2 hardware; online features may require specialized network preservation.

primary.version: North American PS2 release with online multiplayer
primary.why: MotoGP 4 is sourced as a PlayStation 2-only Namco game based on the 2004 MotoGP season. The North American release was delayed to add online multiplayer for up to eight players, making it the most complete regional version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the North American PlayStation 2 release on original hardware or PCSX2; online functionality may require preservation services or original-network-era support.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster; online play availability depends on preservation support.

entries.title: MotoGP '07

emulation.notes: Use PCSX2 or original PlayStation 2 hardware.

primary.why: MotoGP '07 for PlayStation 2 is sourced as the fifth game in this PlayStation-format MotoGP line and the first published by Capcom after Capcom acquired the PlayStation-format rights. It is distinct from the same-year Xbox 360/PC game, which belongs to the THQ format-rights branch.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation 2 version on original hardware or PCSX2 with internal-resolution upscaling.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not conflate with the unrelated 2007 Xbox 360/PC MotoGP game from THQ's rights branch.
